title: Queue from a circular array
statement: Start simple: Build an integer queue with enqueue, dequeue, and size. The oldest value leaves first. Use a circular buffer and grow it without losing order. The theory is optional. The C solution appears after the hidden tests pass.
constraints: dequeue on an empty queue throws IllegalStateException.
think: Head and tail indexes can wrap around the array.
Size distinguishes full from empty when both indexes meet.
On growth, copy from head in queue order into a fresh array.
hints: Use modulo for the next index.
When copying, start at head rather than index zero.

tests.name: fifo
tests.call: { IntQueue q = new IntQueue(); q.enqueue(1); q.enqueue(2); return q.dequeue() + "," + q.dequeue(); }

tests.name: size
tests.call: { IntQueue q = new IntQueue(); q.enqueue(1); q.enqueue(2); return String.valueOf(q.size()); }

tests.name: wrap
tests.call: { IntQueue q = new IntQueue(); q.enqueue(1); q.enqueue(2); q.dequeue(); q.enqueue(3); return q.dequeue() + "," + q.dequeue(); }

tests.name: grow
tests.call: { IntQueue q = new IntQueue(); for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) q.enqueue(i); return q.dequeue() + ":" + q.size(); }

tests.name: drain
tests.call: { IntQueue q = new IntQueue(); q.enqueue(7); q.dequeue(); return String.valueOf(q.size()); }

tests.name: order-after-growth
tests.call: { IntQueue q = new IntQueue(); for (int i = 1; i <= 8; i++) q.enqueue(i); StringBuilder b = new StringBuilder(); while (q.size() > 0) { if (!b.isEmpty()) b.append(','); b.append(q.dequeue()); } return b.toString(); }
